traits.leaf_area_per_basal_area.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 206 poplars and cottonwoods (five species): 0.152 m² of leaf a cm². Median leaf area over trunk area at breast height of its open-grown street and park trees 20 cm or more through, the trees the broadleaf median (0.167) was taken over.

traits.height_growth_rate.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data, open-grown street and park trees: the median height of its 229 poplars of all species (7 age bins, 10 to 102 years) by age bin, fitted (least squares, weighted by trees) as H (1 - exp(-k (age + 3))): k 0.029 a year, H 25.7 m. Bins and fit: plantgen-claude project-files/tree-shape/UTD-SIZES-2026-10-23.md, round5-2026-10-26/tools/utdfit.py (tree shape, 2026-10-27).

traits.crown_spread.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 138 poplars and cottonwoods 25 years or older (five species): 0.77. Median crown width over height of its trees 25 years or older (15 or older where it has fewer than 10 that old), measured open-grown street and park trees.

traits.crown_base_share.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 138 poplars and cottonwoods 25 years or older (five species): 0.17 (quartiles 0.11 and 0.25). Median height of the crown's base over the tree's height of its trees 25 years or older (15 or older where it has fewer than 10 that old), measured open-grown street and park trees, which are often pruned up for clearance.

appearance.bark_look.note: Poplar bark: shoots with dash lenticels, and trunks furrowed into long flat ridges as they age (cottonwoods all over; aspens at the base, their species adding their smooth white stage). Reference: quaking aspen's record (plantgen-claude project-files/bark/records/populus-tremuloides.json); the genus furrows as the aspen's base does, inferred.

traits.short_shoots.note: Hallé, Oldeman and Tomlinson 1978, p. 60: short shoots live a limited time and often fall cleanly at a scar, as in Populus.

traits.perianth.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 257: Salix and Populus are the extreme of the family's floral reduction, their flowers in catkins with no perianth (nectar glands in its place in Salix).
